items.stem: A patient has a low mean arterial pressure, warm extremities, low systemic vascular resistance and high cardiac output after a severe infection. Which shock state best fits?

options.rationale: Correct: low SVR with high/normal cardiac output after infection is characteristic of distributive/septic shock.
Cardiogenic shock typically shows low cardiac output and high SVR, not this pattern.
Hypovolemic shock shows high SVR and low output, not warm extremities with low SVR.
Obstructive shock arises from a mechanical obstruction and does not typically give low SVR with high output.

items.explanation: Correct: low SVR with high/normal cardiac output after infection is characteristic of distributive/septic shock.

items.stem: An arterial blood gas shows low pH, high PaCO2, and a near-normal bicarbonate. This is best described as:

options.rationale: Correct: low pH with elevated PaCO2 and little metabolic compensation indicates acute respiratory acidosis.
Metabolic alkalosis shows high pH and high bicarbonate, not this pattern.
A near-normal bicarbonate and high PaCO2 do not fit metabolic acidosis.
A low pH is not normal acid-base status.

items.explanation: Correct: low pH with elevated PaCO2 and little metabolic compensation indicates acute respiratory acidosis.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that reduce harm in a mechanically ventilated adult in critical care.

options.text: Targeting a light, goal-directed sedation level and assessing daily readiness to wean
options.rationale: Correct: lighter, goal-directed sedation and daily readiness assessment reduce ventilator days and delirium.

options.text: Elevating the head of the bed when not contraindicated
options.rationale: Correct: head-of-bed elevation helps reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia risk.

options.text: Keeping the patient deeply sedated at all times
options.rationale: Routine deep sedation increases delirium and prolongs ventilation.

options.text: Silencing all monitor alarms to reduce noise
options.rationale: Disabling alarms removes a key safety signal.

options.text: Avoiding any assessment of weaning readiness
options.rationale: Skipping weaning assessment prolongs unnecessary ventilation.

items.explanation: Correct: lighter, goal-directed sedation and daily readiness assessment reduce ventilator days and delirium.
